title: How do you get there?
goal: Ask how things are done, and read rules, signs and recipe steps in the passive aorist: nasıl gidilir, içilmez, doğranır.

intro.text: With no subject at all, the passive talks about people in general: *Oraya nasıl gidilir?* (How do you get there?), *Burada sigara içilmez* (No smoking here). Recipes give their steps the same way: *Soğanlar doğranır* (The onions are chopped).

vocab.en: sign (on a road, a door or a shop)

exercises.question: The sign on the door says *Burada sigara içilmez.* What does it mean?

why.2: The aorist states a rule, not a past event.

exercises.explain: *iç-il-mez*: the negative aorist of the passive, a rule for everyone.

exercises.en: How do you get to the station?

reject.why: Harmony: *gid-il-* has i, so the aorist is *-ir*: *gidilir*.
A passive stem has more than one syllable, so its aorist is `-Ir`: *gid-il-ir*.

exercises.hint: Ask in general, for anyone: passive + aorist.
exercises.explain: *git-* softens to *gid-* before the vowel of `-Il`: *gid-il-ir*, **how does one go**.

accept: What do you call this in Turkish?
What is this called in Turkish?
What do you call that in Turkish?
What is that called in Turkish?
How do you say [this|that] in Turkish?

exercises.explain: After a vowel the passive is *-n*; *doğran-* has more than one syllable, so the aorist is *-ır*: *doğra-n-ır*.

exercises.en: You can't take photos in the museum.

exercises.prompt: You don't go into a mosque with your shoes on.

reject.why: *Girmez* is **he doesn't go in**. For people in general, use the passive: *gir-il-mez*.

exercises.en: First the onions are chopped, then they're added to the oil.
exercises.explain: Recipes give their steps in the passive aorist: *doğra-n-ır*, *ekle-n-ir*.

exercises.question: *Bu su içilir mi?* What is the person asking?
options: Is this water safe to drink?

why.1: That would be *Bu suyu içtin mi?*
why.2: That would be *Bu suyu kim içti?*

exercises.explain: *iç-il-ir mi?*: **is this water drunk?**, in general: is it drinkable?

exercises.en: When the water boils, the eggs are added.

exercises.prompt: How do you get to the museum?

accept: In Turkey, guests are offered tea.
In Turkey, a guest is offered tea.
In Turkey, [guests are|a guest is] served tea.
In Turkey, [they|people|you] offer [tea to guests|guests tea].
Guests are offered tea in Turkey.

exercises.prompt: The eggs are boiled for ten minutes.

reject.why: *Haşlar* is active, **(someone) boils**. The eggs are boiled: *haşla-n-ır*.
